t: Under Ind AS 117 the general measurement model for insurance contracts is also known as the:
e: The general measurement model (Building Block Approach) uses fulfilment cash flows plus the contractual service margin.

t: If capital is ₹300 crore and liabilities are ₹1,700 crore, total assets as per the accounting equation are:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Assets = Capital + Liabilities = 300 + 1,700 = ₹2,000 crore.

t: AS 3 classifies cash flows during a period under which three heads?
e: The cash flow statement classifies flows into operating, investing and financing activities.

t: Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013 apply to general insurers:
o: To the extent applicable, with specific modifications to AS 3, AS 13 and AS 17
Only if the insurer is listed
e: AS apply to insurers to the extent applicable, except that AS 3 is direct-method only, AS 13 does not apply and AS 17 applies to all.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: Internal audit is mandated under which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 138 deals with internal audit; Section 177 deals with the Audit Committee.

t: Net claims paid ₹2,000 crore; net outstanding claims at year end ₹3,200 crore and at the beginning ₹3,000 crore. Net Incurred Claims are:
'Other forms of capital' that an insurer may issue under the 2024 Registration and Capital Structure regulations are:
o: Preference share capital and subordinated debt
e: Insurers may raise funds through preference share capital and subordinated debt.

t: An insurer's gross direct premium is ₹2,000 crore, of which Marine Cargo contributes ₹230 crore. Is a separate segment schedule required for Marine Cargo?
o: No, because only the listed segments need separate schedules
Yes, because it contributes 11.5%, more than 10% of gross direct premium
Yes, because every segment above ₹100 crore is shown separately
e: Any other sub-segment contributing more than 10% of total gross direct premium must be shown separately; 230/2,000 = 11.5%.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: Listed equity costing ₹200 crore has a fair value of ₹170 crore on the balance sheet date. The treatment is:
o: No entry, as the loss is unrealised
₹30 crore debited to the Fair Value Change Account
₹30 crore charged to the Profit and Loss Account
₹30 crore charged to the Revenue Account
e: Unrealised losses on actively traded equity are also taken to the FVCA under equity, not through profit.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: Under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938, an insurer may assume a risk only when:
o: The premium is received in advance or guaranteed to be paid in the prescribed manner
The proposal form is signed by the proposer
The policy document has been issued
The agent has collected the premium cheque
e: Section 64VB prohibits assumption of risk unless the premium is received in advance or is guaranteed/deposited as prescribed.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: An officer with existing loans aggregating ₹95 lakh applies for a further housing loan of ₹10 lakh. The application:
o: Can be sanctioned with Board approval only
Can be sanctioned up to ₹2 crore
Cannot be sanctioned in full, as aggregate loans would exceed ₹1 crore
Can be sanctioned as housing loans are outside the cap
e: Aggregate loans to an employee cannot exceed ₹1 crore; 95 + 10 = ₹1.05 crore breaches the limit.

t: Reinsurer balances total ₹200 crore, including ₹30 crore from a foreign reinsurer without an Indian branch outstanding 190 days and ₹20 crore from GIC Re outstanding 300 days. Admissible value for solvency is:
e: The foreign reinsurer balance beyond 180 days is excluded (30); the GIC Re balance is within 365 days and admissible: 200 − 30 = ₹170 crore.

t: Pass book shows a favourable balance of ₹3,20,000. Cheques issued but not presented ₹60,000; cheques deposited but not collected ₹45,000; interest of ₹5,000 credited by bank not recorded in the cash book. Balance as per cash book is:
Net Written Premium ₹2,400 crore; opening UPR ₹1,300 crore; closing UPR ₹1,200 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A release of UPR adds to earned premium: 2,400 − (1,200 − 1,300) = ₹2,500 crore.

t: Assets ₹9,600 crore and liabilities ₹8,100 crore. Capital is:
Net Written Premium ₹2,400 crore and UPR increased by ₹150 crore during the year. Net Earned Premium is:
e: An increase in UPR reduces earned premium: 2,400 − 150 = ₹2,250 crore.

t: Figures in the financial statements of an insurer may be rounded off to the nearest:
e: The general instructions permit rounding off figures to the nearest lakhs.

t: KMP, a term used in the Companies Act and accounting, expands to:
e: KMP refers to Key Management Person(nel) such as the CEO, CFO and Company Secretary.

t: Gross premium written in India ₹8,000 crore; no foreign or rural business. Including the Insurtech and awareness allowance, the maximum expenses of management is:
e: 30% × 8,000 = 2,400; plus 5% × 2,400 = 120 for Insurtech/awareness; total ₹2,520 crore.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: Outstanding claims including IBNR ₹3,000 crore; URR ₹2,500 crore; Catastrophe reserve ₹100 crore; Premium deficiency ₹50 crore; other liabilities ₹400 crore; other assets ₹300 crore. Policyholders' Funds are:
Under the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, Schedule I relates to:
e: Schedule I covers actuarial functions; finance is Schedule II and investment Schedule III.

t: Subordinated debt ₹300 crore, shareholders' funds ₹1,500 crore and profit after tax ₹180 crore. Debt-equity ratio and return on net worth are:
e: Debt-equity = 300 / 1,500 = 0.20; return on net worth = 180 / 1,500 = 12%.

t: Gross claims paid ₹500 crore and reinsurance recoveries on claims ₹120 crore. Net claims paid are:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Net claims = gross claims less reinsurance recoveries = 500 − 120 = ₹380 crore.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: An annual policy with net premium ₹36,500 incepted on 1 January. Under the unexpired-period (1/365) method, the UPR at 31 March (90 days expired, non-leap year) is:
e: Daily premium ₹100; unexpired days 365 − 90 = 275; UPR = 275 × 100 = ₹27,500.
